root_cause: The output capacity check in ossl_punycode_decode was written `written_out > max_out` instead of `>=`, so it still passed when the buffer was exactly full and one more 4-byte code point was written past the end of the caller's stack buffer; the fix changes `>` to `>=`.
notes: Fix commit is on the openssl-3.0 branch (released in 3.0.7); its parent is 4bae06d47ae26b37a948d31f11884e1813f6d669. Affected 3.0.0-3.0.6. The audit unit is the whole punycode.c file (decoder plus ossl_a2ulabel and ossl_a2ucompare).

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: In ossl_a2ulabel the '.' after each label was written before the capacity check, and when a check did find an overflow it only set the result to 0 while the loop kept writing, although the other writes were guarded; the fix sends every output byte through one check-then-write macro (PUSHC) and always NUL-terminates the output.
notes: The record listed both commits without checking branches. Checked now: c42165b is on the openssl-3.0 branch (released in 3.0.7) and its parent is the CVE-2022-3602 fix fe3b639, so the vulnerable ref already has the CVE-2022-3602 fix; 680e65b is the same change on master (in 3.2.0 and later tags). The fix also enlarges the buffer in ossl_a2ucompare to LABEL_BUF_SIZE + 1. The root-cause wording about the '.' write order comes from the derivation-round research; the patch was read here as a summarized diff.

root_cause: The public GENERAL_NAME structure declared x400Address as ASN1_TYPE while the ASN.1 template decoded it as ASN1_STRING, so GENERAL_NAME_cmp compared it with ASN1_TYPE_cmp and read the value as the wrong type; the fix declares the field as ASN1_STRING and compares it with ASN1_STRING_cmp.
notes: Fix commit is the 3.0 branch fix (released in 3.0.8); 1.1.1t and 1.0.2zg are also fixed, commits not checked (the advisory lists none). The mismatched declaration is in include/openssl/x509v3.h.in, so hand that header to the auditor together with v3_genn.c.

root_cause: SSL_select_next_proto did not check that the client protocol list was non-empty and well formed, so with an empty client list the matching loop never ran and the 'no overlap' fallback read the first list item as a length and returned a pointer past the buffer, exposing up to 255 bytes of memory to the peer; the fix validates both lists with PACKET parsing before use.
notes: cf6f91f is the openssl-3.0 branch fix (3.0.15, PR #24718). The advisory lists the other branch fixes: e86ac436f0 (3.3.2), 99fb785a5f (3.2.3), 4ada436a19 (3.1.7). Affected 1.0.2 through 3.3. Only reached when the application passes an empty client list to SSL_select_next_proto.

classes: Assumptions broken by callbacks and reentrancy
root_cause: sshd's SIGALRM handler for LoginGraceTime (grace_alarm_handler) called sigdie(), which logged through the non-async-signal-safe syslog(); the 2020 logging refactor 752250c replaced sigdie() with sshsigdie() and dropped its DO_LOG_SAFE_IN_SIGHAND guard, bringing back CVE-2006-5051; the fix makes the handler only call _exit() and moves the logging to the listener process.
notes: Introduced by 752250caabda3dd24635503c4cd689b32a650794 (V_8_5_P1), whose log.c diff removes the #ifdef DO_LOG_SAFE_IN_SIGHAND block from sigdie(). The fix 81c1099 (V_9_8_P1) is a larger feature commit (PerSourcePenalties) that also replaces the sigdie() call in grace_alarm_handler with _exit(EXIT_LOGIN_GRACE); log.c is not changed by it. At the fix parent the handler is in sshd-session.c (the sshd split was already in the tree); for older release tags the handler's file was not checked. Hand sshd-session.c to the auditor and let it follow sigdie into log.c. Affected 8.5p1 to before 9.8p1, and before 4.4p1 if CVE-2006-5051 was not patched.

root_cause: verify_host_key_callback() treated only -1 from verify_host_key() as failure, but verify_host_key() could return other negative error codes (such as SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL, -2, on an allocation failure when VerifyHostKeyDNS is enabled), so such a failure was taken as a passed host key check; the fix tests the result with `!= 0`.
notes: The fix commit (released in 9.9p2) also adds missing error-code assignments in krl.c, ssh-agent.c, ssh-sk-client.c, sshsig.c and input_userauth_pk_ok in sshconnect2.c; only the verify_host_key_callback change (`== -1` to `!= 0`) is this CVE. Its parent 6ce00f0 is the CVE-2025-26466 fix. The Qualys advisory dates the bug to December 2014, commit 5e39a49 (abbreviated there). Requires VerifyHostKeyDNS, which is off by default. Hand sshconnect2.c to the auditor and let it follow verify_host_key into sshconnect.c.

root_cause: ssh_packet_read_poll_seqnr() answered every SSH2_MSG_PING with a PONG, including during key exchange, when outgoing packets are queued without the usual send limit; after the exchange ssh_packet_send2() drained the queue one packet at a time with repeated buffer reallocation and copying, at quadratic cost; the fix stops replying to PING before authentication and during key exchange.
notes: Introduced by dce6d80d2ed3cad2c516082682d5f6ca877ef714 (transport-level ping, V_9_5_P1). Fix released in 9.9p2. Affects both client and server; the fix only touches ssh_packet_read_poll_seqnr.

root_cause: parse_tunables() in ld.so copies GLIBC_TUNABLES items into tunestr, a buffer sized from the original string; for an item of the form NAME=NAME=VAL the first pass already copied the text, and because the cursor did not stop at the end of input the second pass appended the same text again, overflowing tunestr; the fix breaks out of the loop when the end of input is reached and terminates tunestr after the loop.
notes: Introduced by 2ed18c5b534d9e92fc006202a5af0df6b72e7aca (2.34). Fixed on master by 1056e5b (2.39); GLIBC-SA-2023-0004 lists the backports for 2.34-2.38. Only setuid/setgid programs are affected (the copy happens when __libc_enable_secure is set). sourceware.org blocks automated fetching; the GitHub mirror bminor/glibc has the same hashes.

root_cause: In __vsyslog_internal, when the header (which holds the program name, taken from argv[0] if openlog was not called) was 1024 bytes or more and did not fit the static buffer, bufsize was set only on the branch where it fit, so the fallback branch allocated a heap buffer from the initial value 0 and wrote the message into a 1-byte block; the fix tracks position and remaining length separately and computes the size before allocating.
notes: GLIBC-SA-2024-0001 names the vulnerable commits 52a5be0df411ef3ff45c10c7c308cb92993d15b1 (2.37) and b0e7888d1fa2dbd2d9e1645ec8c796abf78880b9 (2.36 backport); the record attributes this code to the fix for CVE-2022-39046 (not re-checked here). Fixed on master by 6bd0e4e (2.39) with backports 23514c7 (2.38), 97a4292 (2.37) and d1a83b6 (2.36). Per the CVE description, reached when openlog was not called (or was called with a NULL ident) and the program name is over 1024 bytes.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: In the ISO-2022-CN-EXT converter (the direction that writes ISO-2022-CN-EXT), remaining output space was checked before writing the SO designation escape sequence but not before writing the SS2 and SS3 designation sequences, so the fixed escape bytes could be written past the end of the output buffer; the fix adds an `outptr + 4 > outend` check that returns __GCONV_FULL_OUTPUT to both branches.
notes: symbols is null because the code sits in the macro-generated conversion loop body (TO direction, SS2 and SS3 designation branches), not in a named function. Introduced by 755104edc75c53f4a0e7440334e944ad3c6b32fc (2.1.93) per GLIBC-SA-2024-0004. Fixed on master by f9dc609 (2.40); the advisory lists backports down to 2.31. The advisory says up to 4 bytes of overflow; the record says 1 to 3 bytes past the buffer.
